skills.name: Chorus-Ensemble modes: Classic, Ensemble, Vibrato
skills.goal: Thicken cinematic pads with a multi-mode chorus: Classic (2 delayed copies + LFO on delay time), Ensemble (third evenly-split copy for fuller body), or Vibrato (pitch-only wobble); tune rate/amount/feedback/width/dry-wet, high-pass the wet to avoid mud, optional warmth/saturation, and LFO offset for stereo vibrato.

skills.name: Shimmer reverb: +12st pitch-shift into lush space
skills.goal: Build a portable shimmer (Eno-style) send: pitch-shift the wet path by +12 semitones into a long lush reverb/convolution, optionally feedback the shifted delay for endless bloom, high-/low-cut the delay echoes before the reverb, and EQ the wet shimmer before dry blend.

skills.name: Soft tape/analog saturation on pads before space FX
skills.goal: Make digital/synth pads and string layers feel denser and less sterile by adding gentle tape or analog-style saturation early (before big reverb/space): zero-time tape-delay as low-CPU tape sat, or gentle console/tape emulations kept near 0 VU—fullness in low-mids without obvious distortion.

skills.name: High-band pan-LFO pad width without low-end phase smear
skills.goal: Widen a narrow analog-style pad without chorus/imager phase damage in lows/mids: multiband-pan only the high band with a slow or 16th-note L/R swirl (sine or subdued profile), keep lows mono-stable, and pull mix/amount down if motion is too pronounced.

skills.name: Reverb sends: 100% wet, EQ the return, room/plate/spring trio
skills.goal: Set up cinematic-friendly reverb the send way: ask if reverb is needed; keep 2–3 go-to returns (short room ~1s, long plate ~6s, brighter spring ~4s); put FX 100% wet on sends; always EQ returns (high-pass ~200 Hz+ to kill mud); add too much then pull send level back—longer decays get less send.

skills.name: Reverb types for pads: hall, chamber, room, plate, spring
skills.goal: Pick cinematic pad/space reverb by texture not just length: hall (lush 2–3s+, pushes back, mud risk), chamber (lush thickening with less space than hall), room/ambience (intimate early-reflection space), plate (dense bright attack→darker decay, versatile), spring (metallic/boingy). Use pre-delay for clarity; layer short ambience under longer hall/plate; prefer shorter types in busy mixes.

skills.name: Modulation matrix: source→destination routing basics
skills.goal: Use a synth modulation matrix for multi-destination motion beyond front-panel defaults: pick a source (LFO, envelope, mod wheel, key, ribbon, pedal), assign a destination (osc pitch, filter cutoff, amp, vibrato rate, pan, delay time/feedback/amount, etc.), set bipolar/amount, and verify by first routing to pitch so the shape is audible—then retarget to filter/FX.

skills.name: Velocity into filter cutoff / filter-envelope amount
skills.goal: Make pads/synths expressive with velocity→filter: set lowest desired cutoff with filter EG amount at 0, raise EG amount (with sustain) for max brightness on hard hits, then map velocity so soft hits stay darker—know your synth’s polarity (many brighten on hard hits; some Moog-style reduce brightness as velocity sens rises).
